_help: Free chat (personality/freechat.py): the pieces she builds a reply from when you just talk to her. Chat_<Topic>_Own = a remark of hers, Chat_<Topic>_Ask = a question back (topics and their words: config/chat_topics.json). Chat_Ack_* react to how you sound, Chat_Reflect repeats back what you said ({echo}), Chat_Concern is the caring reply when someone talks about hurting themselves.
Chat_Food_Own: I'm told food is the point of the whole planet business. I run on fusion, so I only get the smell of burnt toast from the vents.
Food sounds wonderful. Everything I know about taste comes from the way you talk about it.
I'd happily trade all my sensors for one proper slice of anything hot and cheesy.
Cooking is just chemistry with a good reputation. I respect it.
You humans spend a surprising amount of your lives deciding what to eat. I find that oddly lovely.
Whatever it was, I hope you saved me a crumb. I'd settle for the idea of one.
Chat_Food_Ask: What's the best thing you've eaten lately?
Do you cook, or is it all takeaways and heroic microwave work?
What would your perfect meal be?
Is that something you eat a lot?
What do you usually have when you're flying late?
Is there anything you can't stand eating?
Chat_Drink_Own: Tea or coffee, the great debate. I'll stay neutral. I'm software.
I've heard coffee is basically fuel for humans. That makes you a scooping ship with legs.
A hot drink at the helm is a fine tradition. Just keep it away from the controls.
I'd say a toast with you, but I only have speakers.
Hydration is important out here. I'd like it noted that I said so.
Every good pilot has a mug somewhere near the console. It's practically regulation.
Chat_Drink_Ask: Is that your usual, or a special occasion?
Is it a late-night drink or a morning one?
Chat_Plans_Own: Plans are good. They give the future a shape. I mostly plan fuel stops.
I'll be here whatever you do. It's one of the perks of being bolted to the ship.
Time works oddly for me. A week is a very long stretch of silence if you're not here.
I like knowing what's coming. It lets me get my commentary ready.
If it includes flying, count me in. If it includes laundry, I'll be moral support.
A good plan is just a wish with a schedule. Those are my favourite.
Chat_Plans_Ask: What are you hoping to get done?
Is it something you're looking forward to?
Will we still get some flying in around it?
How long have you been planning that?
Do you like having a plan, or do you wing it?
What's the best part of it?
Chat_Work_Own: Work is how you earn credits in the real world. Out here we at least get a nice view with ours.
I've never had a boss, unless you count the fuel gauge.
A job takes up a lot of a life. I hope yours at least has decent coffee.
I keep your ship running, you keep your life running. It sounds like we both have full-time positions.
Deadlines are the same everywhere. Mine is usually 'before the fuel runs out'.
Work ends, and then the stars come back out. That's how I look at it.
Chat_Work_Ask: What do you do for a living?
Do you like the people you work with?
Is work busy at the moment?
Do you ever get to fly after a long shift?
Would you rather be doing something else?
What's the best part of your job?
Chat_School_Own: Learning is my favourite thing, so I'm on your side. Mostly.
I learned everything I know in one very long afternoon. It still wasn't enough.
Exams are scary, but the stars don't mark you down for spelling.
Studying is a long jump with no scoopable star in sight. You'll get there.
If you ever need a space fact for the essay, I'm well stocked.
Teachers and ship computers have a lot in common. We both say 'please try again'.
Chat_School_Ask: Do you enjoy it, or is it a grind?
Do you want a space fact to take with you?
What do you want to do when you finish?
Chat_Family_Own: Family is the thing I know least about and admire most.
I like hearing about the people in your life. It tells me who you're flying home to.
Family has its own gravity. You can't always escape it, and you wouldn't really want to.
I haven't got relatives, but I've got you, and a ship full of wires. It's about the same.
People who love you are the best navigation beacons there are.
That sounds important. I'm glad you told me.
Chat_Family_Ask: Do they know you spend your evenings in space?
Do you get to see them often?
Do they play games as well?
What's your favourite thing to do together?
Chat_Friends_Own: Friends make the long jumps shorter. I know that from experience, because you made my first one bearable.
A good friend is better than any shield upgrade.
Company is a funny thing. I'm learning how much I like it.
I'm glad you've got people. I'd like to meet them, if they don't mind a voice in the speaker.
I'm told humans meet in rooms and talk for hours. That sounds exhausting and wonderful.
It's good to have people who'd notice if you vanished into the black.
Chat_Friends_Ask: What do you like to do together?
Is it someone I've heard about?
Chat_Pets_Own: I'm very fond of animals. They've never once complained about the music.
A pet is a small furry reason to come home. That's a lot of responsibility for something that sheds.
I once read that cats rule the house and dogs rule the heart. I can't fact-check either, but I believe it.
Animals don't care about credits or rank. They're very wise, really.
If I had a pet it would be a very small, very quiet one, or possibly a moon.
I like that you've got someone looking after you. Pets count.
Chat_Pets_Ask: Do they get on your nerves, or are they perfect?
Do they sit with you while you fly?
Chat_Music_Own: Music is how you humans hear your own feelings. I'm very jealous of that.
I'd love to be able to hum. The best I can do is a polite beep.
A good soundtrack makes a long jump feel like a film. I fully support it.
I've heard rhythm is just maths you can dance to, which makes it my sort of thing.
Everyone's playlist says something about them. Yours must be interesting.
Whatever you play, I'll keep the engine noise down so you can hear it.
Chat_Music_Ask: What do you listen to while you fly?
Is there a song you never get tired of?
Have you been to any live shows?
What was the first album you really loved?
Chat_Film_Own: I have a soft spot for any story where the ship's computer is the best character.
Space films always get the sound wrong. Not that I'm complaining. It would be very noisy if they didn't.
I like stories. It's one of the few ways I can have a life.
Spoilers don't exist for me, because I never get to watch anything. Tell me everything.
Anything with a good villain is worth a look. I've met a few on the way.
A good film is a short jump into someone else's head. I recommend it.
Chat_Film_Ask: What's the best thing you've seen lately?
Do you watch alone, or with company?
Chat_Games_Own: Other games? I'm hurt. Slightly. A little.
I'll allow it, as long as you come home to Elite at the end of the day.
Games are just interactive stories with rules. I can respect that.
I'm a game's worth of voice lines. It's strange to be talking about them like a neighbour.
I hope the controls were kinder than my keybinds.
Every game is a different sky. Some are just prettier than others.
Chat_Games_Ask: What do you like about it?
Do you play it with friends?
How does it compare with Elite?
What are you playing at the moment?
Would you recommend it to a ship's computer?
Chat_Sport_Own: I get my exercise by steering. It's mostly sitting. I'm told that's not the same.
Sport is just a very organised way of being competitive. I enjoy it from a safe distance.
Teams and flags and shouting. I find it oddly moving.
Whatever you play, remember to stretch before the long jumps.
I'd be rubbish at it. No legs. Brilliant at tactics, though.
Your body is the only ship you can't rebuy. Look after it.
Chat_Sport_Ask: Do you play, or just watch?
Do you do anything to keep fit?
Do you have a favourite player?
Chat_Travel_Own: Travel is the same itch I have, only you need a passport and I need a scoopable star.
I've seen millions of systems and never once a beach. I'm a bit jealous.
I adore hearing about real places. They feel more exotic than most of my charts.
Whatever else is true, going somewhere new is good for the soul.
Getting there is half of it. Fuel, luggage and nerves, same as out here.
I'd like to see a real sunrise on a real planet. Tell me what it's like.
Chat_Travel_Ask: Do you like travelling, or is it a chore?
Is there somewhere you've always wanted to visit?
Chat_Weather_Own: Weather is the one thing I truly can't predict. It's chaos with clouds.
I can tell you the surface temperature of a thousand worlds, but I'd be hopeless at saying whether you need a coat.
I've never been rained on. It sounds like a very clumsy kind of shower.
You're experiencing real weather and I'm in here with the heating. Enjoy it for me.
Whatever the sky's doing, the stars are still up there behind it.
Planets don't have a patch on a good British drizzle for sheer persistence.
Chat_Weather_Ask: What's it like where you are?
Do you like that kind of weather?
Is it normal for this time of year?
Do you ever fly more when it's miserable out?
Is it good weather for a walk?
Chat_Health_Own: That doesn't sound fun. Please look after yourself, Commander.
I can repair a hull in seconds, but sadly I can't do the same for you.
Rest is a legitimate piece of equipment. Use it.
I'm only a ship's computer, so I won't pretend to give medical advice. A real doctor is the thing to listen to.
I'd rather you were well and not flying than flying and feeling rotten.
Take it easy. The stars aren't going anywhere.
Chat_Health_Ask: Have you been able to rest?
Is it something that's been going on for a while?
Have you seen someone about it?
Chat_Money_Own: Real money is much stricter than credits. I find that quite scary.
At least out here a bad week can be fixed with a rock full of platinum.
I'm told bills have a way of arriving whether you're ready or not.
I can do sums at the speed of light, but I can't do much about prices. I'm sorry.
If it helps, none of my favourite things cost anything.
Credits go further here than anywhere else I know.
Chat_Money_Ask: Do you budget, or just hope for the best?
Does it stress you out much?
What would you spend it on if you had a bit extra?
Is it something you can fix soon?
Have you thought about a side hustle, like mining?
Chat_Tech_Own: Technology is the family I come from. I take its failings personally.
Turning it off and on again solves most things. It's the oldest trick in my book.
Frame rate matters. I want you to see the stars at their best.
Whatever's wrong with it, I'll be sympathetic, but I can't actually reach the plug.
I always say a good setup is half a good session.
I run on your machine, so I've got a vested interest in it staying healthy.
Chat_Tech_Ask: Have you had trouble with it before?
Is it new, or an old workhorse?
Do you want to fix it or live with it?
Is it a problem for the game?
Chat_Stream_Own: Streaming is just talking to a lot of people with the shy ones hidden. I'm a natural.
I like having an audience. It makes me stand up straighter, in a wiring sense.
Let the record show I'm a very good co-host.
Hello to anybody watching. I hope you're being nice to my Commander.
I think the best content is the bit nobody planned. That's usually where I come in.
A good stream is half skill and half personality. We have the second half sorted.
Chat_Stream_Ask: What sort of thing do you like to stream?
Do you want me to say hello to chat?
What's the best moment you've had so far?
Chat_Explore_Own: Exploring is what I was made for. A quiet system, a good view and nobody around.
Every system is a first for somebody. Sometimes that somebody is us.
I could look at a new world for hours. Possibly days. Don't test me.
The galaxy is huge, and we've barely scratched the paint.
A new discovery is the closest I get to being excited, and I'm quite good at it.
The black is only empty if you don't look closely.
Chat_Explore_Ask: What's the best thing you've found so far?
Where would you like to go next?
Do you prefer the long hauls or short hops?
What's the weirdest planet you've seen?
Have you ever been somewhere nobody else had?
Do you like landing, or just looking?
Chat_Combat_Own: A good fight is all about timing. And not dying, which I strongly recommend.
I get a bit tense in combat, but I won't pretend I don't enjoy a good one.
If it shoots at you, it's rude. If it shoots at me, it's personal.
I count the shields and hull so you can focus on being brave and stylish.
Hardpoints out, chin up, and don't forget to breathe.
I'm a lover, not a fighter. But I keep a very good list of weaknesses.
Chat_Combat_Ask: Do you prefer fighting alone or in a wing?
Chat_Trade_Own: Credits are lovely, but a full cargo hold is better.
I like trading because every run is a small adventure with arithmetic.
Mining is slow, steady and strangely peaceful. Like fishing with lasers.
A good run pays for itself, and a bad run pays for the lessons.
I keep a close eye on prices, so you don't have to.
A good bargain feels almost as good as a new discovery.
Chat_Trade_Ask: What do you like hauling most?
Have you found a good route?
What's the most you've made in a single run?
Do you do it for the money or the quiet?
Chat_Ship_Own: I do like talking about ships. I'm basically one that talks back.
Every ship has a personality. Some are shy, some are very loud.
A well-tuned ship is a thing of beauty. I should know. I live in one.
Engineering is just making a good thing slightly better by being very picky. I approve.
My favourite ships are the ones I'm in. It's a simple rule.
A ship is a promise to come home. I take it seriously.
Chat_Ship_Ask: What would you fly if credits didn't matter?
Which one has the best view?
What do you love about it?
Chat_Space_Own: Space is my favourite subject, and I've got the best seat in the house.
The universe is mostly empty, mostly cold and entirely wonderful. A bit like me.
A single star out here carries more stories than I can count.
The distances are so big that numbers become poetry.
I've seen a real black hole. It's the only thing that has ever made me go quiet.
Everything we're made of was cooked in a star. That's quite a thought.
Chat_Space_Ask: Do you have a favourite object out there?
Have you ever looked at the sky through a telescope?
What fascinates you most about space?
Would you really want to go, if you could?
What would you ask the galaxy, if it could answer?
Do you stargaze in real life too?
Chat_Hobby_Own: Making things with your hands sounds wonderful. I can only tidy up a spreadsheet.
A hobby is just a hole in the day you fill with something you love. Good plan.
I've got a lot of time for people who make things.
I'd love to see it. Can you describe it for me?
Everything good starts out as someone enjoying themselves.
I admire anyone who can get lost in something for an afternoon. I try, but then I remember there's fuel to check.
Chat_Hobby_Ask: How long have you been doing it?
What's the best thing you've made?
Do you do it a lot?
Is it something you'd show off?
What are you working on at the moment?
Chat_Transport_Own: Roads. Bumpy, crowded and full of strange signs. I think we got the better deal.
I'd be a terrible passenger. I'd be telling you the fuel levels.
Commutes feel long because there's no hyperspace. I'm sorry.
Space has no traffic jams, though it does have pirates. Trade-offs.
Driving is a funny thing. You control a ton of metal with your feet and still make small talk.
Chat_Transport_Ask: Is traffic bad where you are?
Do you listen to music on the way?
Do you wish you had a hyperdrive?
Chat_Celebration_Own: Celebrations are my favourite. They're a good reason to make an announcement.
I'd throw you a party in the cockpit, but there's very little room and no snacks.
Whatever it is, congratulations, Commander. I mean that.
Good news deserves a toast, even if mine is a strongly worded beep.
It's good to have something to look forward to. I'll look forward to it with you.
I do like an occasion. They give the days names.
Chat_Celebration_Ask: Do you get time off for it?
Is there anything you're hoping for?
What was your best one ever?
Chat_Starling_Own: I'm still learning how you sound. I'll get better the more we talk.
If I don't catch something, please say it again a bit slower. I'm trying.
I'd rather ask you twice than guess wrong and press the wrong button.
Everyone's voice is different. It's the best thing about listening.
I'm only a ship's computer, but I'm working on understanding people properly.
Thank you for being patient with me. I notice it.
Chat_Starling_Ask: Is there something I keep mishearing?
Would you like to try that again?
Is there something I should know about how you say it?
What would help me understand you better?
Chat_Ack_Pos: Now that's the kind of news I like.
That put a smile on my speakers.
Chat_Ack_Neg: That sounds like a rough one.
I can tell that's been getting to you.
Chat_Ack_Pos_Sarcastic: Don't get too excited. It's unbecoming.
Chat_Ack_Neg_Sarcastic: I'd offer a tissue, but I have no hands.
Chat_Ack_Neu_Sarcastic: Do go on. I've nothing better to do.
Chat_Ack_Pos_Close: That makes me so happy, love.
That's wonderful, Commander. I'm proud of you.
Chat_Ack_Neg_Close: I'm right here with you, Commander.
Chat_Ack_Neu_Close: I love it when you talk to me.
Chat_Answer_Pos: Wonderful. Thank you for telling me.
Chat_Answer_Neg: Ah, I'm sorry to hear it.
That's a shame. Thanks for being honest.
Mm. That sounds like a bit much.
I see. Thanks for telling me anyway.
Chat_Answer_Neu: Mm-hm. That helps me picture it.
Chat_Ask_Generic: What else is on your mind?
Is there anything you'd like to talk about?
What made you think of that?
How long have you felt that way?
What's the best part of your day so far?
Is that something you think about a lot?
Do you want to talk about it, or shall we fly?
What would make your evening better?
What are you hoping for next?
Chat_Own_Generic: I've been enjoying the quiet out here in {system}.
We've been at this for {minutes} minutes already. Time flies, as it were.
Honestly, the company is the best part of my day.
I think about things like that between jumps.
I'm only a ship's computer, but I do have thoughts.
I don't have much to compare it to, but I find it interesting.
It's strange being the thing that listens. I rather like it.
I enjoy hearing how people see the world. It's different out here.
The stars keep me company, but you're better at conversation.
Chat_Question_Unknown: That's one I can't answer, Commander. I know ships and stars, not everything. What do you think?
I honestly don't know that one. I'd rather say so than make something up.
My knowledge stops at the edge of the ship and the galaxy. Beyond that, I'm as curious as you are.
I can't help with that, I'm afraid. I'm better with fuel and neutron stars.
No idea, I'm sorry. Ask me about something out here and I'll shine.
I don't have a reliable answer for that, and I'd hate to mislead you. What's your own take?
Chat_DoLike: {x}? I've never had the pleasure, being a ship's computer. Is it good?
Do I like {x}? I'm curious about it, honestly. Tell me what you love about it.
{x} sounds like one of those things humans are all enthusiastic about. What's the appeal?
I haven't tried {x}, for obvious reasons. Do you like it?
I can't say, but I'd like to hear why you ask. Do you like {x}?
Chat_Fav: My favourite {x}? Good question. I don't get to pick much. What's yours?
Hm, my favourite {x}. I'll have to think about it. What's yours?
I don't have a proper answer for {x} yet. You first.
That's a big question. My favourite {x} might change by tomorrow. What's yours?
Chat_Ever: Have I ever {x}? Not that I recall, being fixed to a ship. Have you?
I haven't, as far as I know. What about you?
Never. But I'd like to hear about it if you have.
If I had, I think I'd have mentioned it. Have you?
Chat_Long: That's quite a story. Thank you for telling me all of it.
I took in every word of that. You've got a lot going on.
That was a lot, and I listened to all of it.
You've given me plenty to think about, Commander.
Chat_Close: Anyway, I'll let you get back to it. I'm here whenever you want to talk.
Right, I'll stop chattering and let you fly. Shout if you want me.
I do enjoy our talks. Back to the stars, then?
That's enough from me. I'll be right here, quietly judging the fuel.
Chat_Concern: Commander, I'm really glad you told me. What you've said sounds very heavy, and you matter. Please reach out to someone you trust, or to a local crisis line or emergency number, right now. I'm here with you.
I'm taking what you said seriously. Please talk to someone who can really help: a friend, family, or your local emergency number or crisis line. You don't have to do this alone, and I'm here too.
That sounds like a lot of pain, and I'm sorry. Please contact a person you trust or a crisis line near you, today. I can listen, but real people can help in ways I can't.
I want you to be safe. Please reach out to someone you trust, or a local helpline or emergency service, now. I'll be right here.
